questions.q: What can a Before Business Rule do that an After Business Rule cannot?
options: Read fields on the current record
Be set to run on the update operation
Run JavaScript at all
Call current.setAbortAction(true) to cancel the database write before it happens
questions.explain: Because a Before rule runs before the write, it can still cancel the operation entirely. By the time an After rule runs, the write already succeeded.

questions.q: Look at this Business Rule script. Given the call to setAbortAction, what must its 'When' setting be?
options: After
Before
Display
Async
questions.explain: setAbortAction only has an effect in a Before rule, since only a Before rule runs ahead of the actual database write.

questions.q: Why do After Business Rules commonly update OTHER related records rather than the triggering record itself?
options: Because the triggering record is already safely saved by the time an After rule runs, making it safe to act on related data
Because After rules cannot read the current record at all
Because After rules run before the database write completes
Because updating the current record in an After rule deletes it
questions.explain: After rules run once the write has committed, so the main record is already durable — the natural next step is touching related data.

questions.q: Why does an Async Business Rule exist, given that After rules already run post-write?
options: Async rules cannot access the current record at all
Async is simply a renamed version of the Before timing
Async work is queued and runs in the background, so slow operations don't delay the user's save
Async rules run before the database write, just like Before rules
questions.explain: Async exists specifically so slower operations — notifications, integrations, heavy calculations — don't make the user wait for their save to finish.

questions.q: What is the real purpose of a Display Business Rule?
options: Queuing a slow operation to run in the background after save
Running after the database write to update related records
Passing server-side-computed data to the client via g_scratchpad when the form loads, since it runs before the page renders
Validating a field's format before the record is saved
questions.explain: Display rules run on form load, not on save, and their standard pattern is writing values onto g_scratchpad so client scripts can read server-computed data without a round trip.
